title: 1950 AHSME Problem 32
statement: A \(25\) foot ladder is placed against a vertical wall of a building. The foot of the ladder is \(7\) feet from the base of the building. If the top of the ladder slips \(4\) feet, then the foot of the ladder will slide:

solutions.text:
The initial height, in feet, is \[ \sqrt{25^2-7^2}=\sqrt{576}=24. \] After the top slips, the height is \(20\) feet, so the new horizontal distance is \(\sqrt{25^2-20^2}=15\) feet. The foot therefore slides \(15-7=8\) feet.

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Find the ladder’s original height on the wall using a right triangle
After the top slips, the new height is \(4\) feet less while the hypotenuse stays \(25\)
